summary.overview: OmniScribe has an exceptional context map and layered CI, but the web OCR path does not wire the shared circuit-breaker registry, the highest-churn scripts directory lacks mechanical protection, and session evidence is too sparse to evaluate learning capture.

dimensions.label: Task Understanding
dimensions.summary: AGENTS.md and ARCHITECTURE.md provide thorough context routing, pipeline diagrams, a 60-row key-files table, and explicit Known Tech Debt, but no session-observed task episodes confirm applied understanding.

dimensions.label: Controlled Execution
dimensions.summary: Makefile exposes setup, run, test, doctor, and clean; dev.py implements a graded doctor check; security middleware enforces auth, upload limits, rate limiting, and SSRF fail-closed. Inspected but not session-exercised.

dimensions.label: Change Validation
dimensions.summary: CI runs ruff, mypy, and pytest on every PR with a nightly slow tier, but the highest-churn scripts directory is excluded from lint and untested, OCR failure handlers use bare f-string logging, and architecture boundaries lack a drift gate.

dimensions.label: Reliable Delivery
dimensions.summary: PR-gated CI and release automation exist, but the circuit-breaker registry is not wired into the web OCR path, and in-memory state bounds recovery to process lifetime.

dimensions.label: Learning Capture
dimensions.summary: The 30-day session window yielded zero admitted candidate episodes (one self-analysis session omitted by policy), leaving Learning Capture not evaluable; the evidence boundary retains this unobserved gap.

findings.title: Circuit-breaker sharing is documented but not wired in the web OCR path
findings.reason: The CircuitBreakerRegistry docstring promises process-wide breaker sharing across HTTP requests, but the web OCR pipeline factory constructs OCRProcessor without injecting the shared registry, so each request gets a private breaker. A breaker tripped by one request is invisible to the next request against the same dead endpoint — fail-fast protection is bounded to a single multi-page job, not across requests.
expectedOutput: The web OCR pipeline factory injects the shared registry so a tripped breaker is visible across HTTP requests against the same endpoint.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
Wire the shared circuit-breaker registry into the web OCR path so breakers are visible across requests.

In the OCR pipeline factory, import get_default_circuit_breaker_registry from the resilience module and pass it as the circuit_breaker_registry argument when constructing OCRProcessor. The function already exists and returns a process-wide singleton.

## Validation

- Run the OCR resilience tests: uv run pytest tests/test_ocr_resilience.py -v
- Run the circuit breaker registry tests: uv run pytest tests/test_circuit_breaker_registry.py -v
- Confirm that two OCRProcessor instances constructed with the same api_base and model share the same breaker

findings.title: Highest-churn directory (scripts/) has no lint or test coverage
findings.reason: The scripts directory is the evidence-pack top core candidate (score 70, 19 commits, high churn) and directly imports core internals such as HybridAligner, OCRProcessor, and PDFHandler, yet is excluded from ruff and has zero tests. A core API signature change breaks these debug and visualization tools silently with no CI signal, leaving an agent without working diagnostic tooling when an OCR problem arises.
expectedOutput: A CI-visible check catches core API signature changes that break the scripts directory before an agent reaches for a broken diagnostic tool.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
Add minimal mechanical protection for the scripts directory so core API changes are caught before the tools break silently.

Either add a smoke-import test that verifies each script can be imported without AttributeError, or add a targeted lint pass for scripts with relaxed rules. The existing extend-exclude in pyproject.toml documents why scripts are excluded; keep the production lint surface clean while adding a separate check.

## Validation

- Run the new script-import smoke test: uv run pytest tests/test_scripts_smoke.py -v
- Confirm ruff check src tests still passes unchanged

findings.title: OCR failure handlers use bare logging.warning with f-strings
findings.reason: The hybrid OCR engine uses bare import logging; logging.warning(f-string) in three per-page and per-box failure handlers instead of a module-level logger, and G004 (f-string logging) is globally ignored. An agent debugging a failed multi-page job cannot correlate a WebSocket warning frame back to a specific retry or backoff log line, and the f-string calls bypass any future structured-logging adapter.
expectedOutput: OCR failure handlers use the module logger with lazy formatting so log lines are correlatable and compatible with structured-logging adapters.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
Replace bare logging.warning(f-string) calls with module-logger calls using lazy formatting in the hybrid OCR engine.

Add a module-level logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) at the top of the hybrid engine module. Replace the three bare logging.warning(f-string) calls in the per-page, per-box, and refine failure handlers with logger.warning calls using percent-style formatting. Keep the same message content.

## Validation

- Run ruff check on the hybrid engine module: uv run ruff check src/omniscribe/core/workflows/hybrid.py
- Run the hybrid workflow tests: uv run pytest tests/test_workflows_hybrid.py -v

findings.title: Architecture boundaries are documented but not mechanically enforced
findings.reason: The repo-hygiene test mechanically pins infra-file shape (Dockerfile, compose, pre-commit, nightly, pyproject extras), but the ARCHITECTURE.md Change Blueprint module boundaries and single-responsibility table have no drift gate. A refactor that violates a documented boundary passes CI unless a behavioral test happens to assert that shape.
expectedOutput: A CI-visible test catches documented architecture-boundary violations before a refactor lands.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
Add a lightweight architecture-boundary assertion to the repo-hygiene test suite.

In the existing test_repo_hygiene.py, add assertions that verify key single-responsibility invariants from ARCHITECTURE.md, such as the OCR router not importing workflow internals directly, or the state module remaining a singleton boundary. Focus on the few boundaries most likely to drift during refactoring.

## Validation

- Run the repo hygiene tests: uv run pytest tests/test_repo_hygiene.py -v
- Confirm the new assertions fail when a boundary violation is introduced

findings.title: In-memory job and artifact state is lost on restart with no recovery path
findings.reason: Job history, text and metadata and export artifacts, the OCR queue, and progress channels are process-local singletons. A restart loses all in-flight work with no durable recovery or horizontal-scaling path. This is explicitly documented as Known Tech Debt but has a real consequence for any deployment beyond single-process local desktop use.
expectedOutput: The state module documents its process-lifetime recovery boundary so an operator or agent does not assume durable job state.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
Document the recovery boundary explicitly in the state module so the next operator knows the process-lifetime limit.

In the state module, add a module-level docstring that names the in-memory singletons, states the process-lifetime boundary, and points to the Known Tech Debt section in AGENTS.md. This does not change behavior; it makes the recovery limit discoverable at the owner.

## Validation

- Run mypy on the state module: uv run mypy src/omniscribe/api/routers/state.py
- Confirm the docstring is present and references the Known Tech Debt section
